column1: # Surface classification. ONE reader: scripts/resolve-surface.sh. doctor.sh asks
# it about the whole tree; scripts/gates/surface-resolution.sh asks it about a
# change set. Procedures that need to know how much experimentation a surface
# takes read the answer from it too, rather than re-parsing this file — two
# readers of one table eventually disagree, and the disagreement arrives as a
# green tick on a file nobody classified.
# If you add a FIELD, teach the script to read it in the same change. Config
# nothing reads is worse than none, because it looks like enforcement to
# anyone skimming.
# TWO AXES, and conflating them is a real error:
#   risk     = blast radius if the OUTPUT is wrong. Drives where to experiment.
#   approval = who must sign off on the DIFF. Drives review.
# A draft can be low risk and still need a human before it is sent.
# high   — reaches someone outside the team, or changes how every future
#          output is judged. An unproven approach does not belong here.
# medium — shapes work that will reach someone, with a person in between.
# low    — costs nothing if it is wrong. This is where to experiment.
# Anything unmatched is treated as HIGH / owner. Fail closed: an unclassified
# surface is exactly where damage goes unnoticed. That sentence sat here with
# nothing behind it until v0.12.0 — doctor proved every PATTERN matched a file
# and never asked whether every FILE matched a pattern, and 30 of the 51 files
# in this template matched none, every gate script among them.
# PATTERNS MUST BE DISJOINT. A file matching two rows is an error, not a
# priority puzzle: risk has a maximum but approval does not, so picking a
# winner invents policy. That rules out a broad fallback with narrow overrides
# — `learning/*` alongside `learning/corpus/*` fails — which is why the two
# loose files under learning/ are named individually below.
# `*` CROSSES `/`, matching find -path, so foundations/* covers
# foundations/a/b.md. Approval is a closed vocabulary: owner, reviewer, none.
# pattern

column5: what it requires

column1: # The rows below classify the HARNESS's own files. They are the floor, not the
# job: add a row for every surface the WORK lands on before calling this done.
# Four rows that all point at directories the template created will satisfy
# doctor's coverage check while nothing real has been classified at all.
foundations/*
column4: what the AI must not invent — everything derives from it
column5: Logged approval. Never edited mid-task.

column1: learning/corpus/*
column4: the spec every future output is judged against
column5: Validate with the owner. Logged approval.

column1: learning/reviews/*
column4: findings that drive what the harness becomes
column5: Finding lines must be machine-comparable — see the README there.

column1: contracts/*
column4: the definition of done
column5: Logged approval.

column1: rubrics/*
column4: the articulated standard work is judged against
column5: Logged approval on adoption. Prose until then.

column1: procedures/*
column4: shapes output that will reach someone
column5: A person reads the output before it is sent.

column1: capabilities/*
column4: external instructions or code a runtime may execute
column5: Intake record, immutable pin or content hash, licence review and owner approval.

column1: memory/*
column4: operational notes, consumed by us
column5: Experiment freely.

column1: runs/*
column4: dated output, reviewed before anything leaves
column5: This is where to experiment first.

column1: read-first.md
column4: decides what an agent reads before each kind of task
column5: A person reads new rows. Each row names the failure that justified it.

column1: AGENTS.md
column4: loads into every session — it changes how every future output is judged
column5: Logged approval. Budgeted; see loading-order.md.

column1: GOVERNANCE.md
column4: the authority chain — who may decide what
column5: Logged approval. Never edited in the same change as the work it governs.

column1: loading-order.md
column4: decides what is in the context window before anyone types
column5: Logged approval. Budget re-checked.

column1: harness.yaml
column4: the single adaptation point — every script reads it
column5: Logged approval. Add a key only with a reader in the same change.

column1: capabilities-lock.json
column4: the provenance and reviewed bytes of external capabilities
column5: Append or re-pin only through capability intake. Never accept unexplained hash drift.

column1: config/*
column4: the classification everything else is judged against, this file included
column5: Logged approval. A wrong lane here is invisible everywhere else.

column1: scripts/*
column4: the enforcement itself — a loosened gate looks exactly like a passing one
column5: Logged approval. Prove the gate can still fail: scripts/gate-selftest.sh.

column1: .gitignore
column4: decides what is tracked, and every data-boundary rule reads tracked files
column5: Logged approval. An ignored file is a file no gate can see.

column1: .pii-allow
column4: the exception list for the data boundary — each line switches a rule off
column5: Logged approval per line, with the review that cleared it.

column1: evidence/*
column4: the approval record — whoever edits it can grant themselves approval
column5: Logged approval. Append-only in practice; never rewritten to fit.

column1: decisions/*
column4: the record of a decision already taken elsewhere
column5: A person reads it against the decision it claims to record.

column1: learning/candidates.md
column4: the ratchet queue — what the harness might become
column5: A person reads it before anything is promoted out of it.

column1: learning/changelog.md
column4: what the harness became, and when
column5: A person reads it. Entries are appended, not amended.

column1: learning/retros.md
column4: the record that the improvement loop ran, and what it measured
column5: Appended at every retro, including the ones that changed nothing.

column1: learning/findings.md
column4: what each finding taught, and where the lesson now lives — the recurrence record
column5: Appended, never amended. A person confirms any lesson that becomes a rule, rubric or gate.

column1: learning/journal/*
column4: raw session notes, read at retro
column5: Roles, never names. Nothing here applies until a retro promotes it.

column1: .claude/*
column4: generated runtime files — the real approval is on the procedures they come from
column5: Regenerate, never hand-edit: scripts/sync-skills.sh. The skills-sync gate checks it.

column1: README.md
column4: what a human reads to understand this harness
column5: A person reads it. Stale docs are how a harness stops being believed.
